name: The Wooley household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: wooley_jeddiah

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 July 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-07-02, 1 day later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-07-16 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Jeddiah Wooley' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 34, reprinted over 3 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-02 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: La Salle land-sale records list Jeddiah Wooley repeatedly June 16-17, 1835; a U.S. Supreme Court record preserves an August 8, 1835 Chicago land-office receipt in his name. Land purchases and use of the Chicago land office do not establish a Chicago household or residence.

candidates.basis: Exact-name 1835 Illinois land transactions and Chicago land-office receipt.
conflicts: Transactions do not prove Chicago residence.

merge_ruling.for_merge: Jeddiah and Jedidiah are one biblical forename written short and long, the surname agrees letter for letter, the town holds only these two Wooleys, and T-0481 found the La Salle land-sale records listing a Jeddiah Wooley repeatedly on 16-17 June 1835 — a fortnight before the scene date.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE TAX ENTRY IS A JUNIOR, SO THE TOWN HELD TWO MEN OF THE LONGER NAME. The 1833 tax list reads 'Wooley, Jedidiah Jr.', and a roll that troubles to write Jr. is a roll telling us a senior of the same name existed; the letter-list 'Jeddiah Wooley' of 2 July 1834 (#c034) could be either of them, and a fold would have to choose. No printing sets both spellings: a tax roll against a post-office return, which never touch. Neither card is an anchor — no trade, no street, no household on either. D8, and the Jr. is the fact that keeps it there.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
